subject: Reader Rewards: Promo codes for TechDigest Spring Roundup
messages:
From: Susan Kline <susan.kline@techdigest.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: newsletter@techdigest.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Promo codes for our Spring Roundup — quick ask

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you’re well — we’re putting the Spring Roundup newsletter together for early May (expected audience ~45k readers). The editorial team wants to include a small reader perk: a set of one-time promo codes for Redwood that we can reward to engaged readers (sign-ups, survey completions).

Two quick questions:
- What sort of promo credit denominations do you recommend for discovery/demo ops?
- Any restrictions (expiry, per-account limits) we should set so it doesn’t get abused?

We’d like to finalize language and a sample code block by next Tuesday if possible. I can share the campaign brief if that helps.

Thanks — Susan
Susan Kline
Partnerships Editor, TechDigest Media
newsletter@techdigest.ai

---
Attachments: CampaignBrief_SpringRoundup_v1.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Susan Kline <susan.kline@techdigest.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Promo codes for our Spring Roundup — quick ask

Hi Susan — great to hear from you and congrats on the roundup stats. We’d love to participate. Quick thoughts:

- Recommendation: 50 one-time promo codes, each worth $75 in platform credits. It’s large enough for a short proof-of-concept integration (30–60 minutes of usage) but small enough to limit cost exposure.
- Expiry: 90 days from issuance.
- Per-account limit: one code per company (we can tie codes to email domains if you want stricter control).
- Redemption tracking: we’ll provide a CSV of codes and a short UTM'd landing link so you can track clicks and conversions.

I’ve looped in Laura (CS/finance) and Aditya (legal) for a quick OK on limits and T&Cs — they can chime in on any constraints. If that all sounds good I’ll generate the codes and send a CSV with a small blurb and an example call-to-action.

Also — happy to provide a smaller batch of 200 single-use $25 codes instead if you’d prefer to reward more readers at smaller value.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Phone: +1-415-555-0123

Vanessa / team —

Finance ok with either option but prefer the 200x $25 approach for better distribution; lower unit value avoids large spikes on free accounts. A couple of operational asks:

- Please add a hard expiry (90 days) and a redemption cap per account (one per billing account).
- Mark codes as "promo_newsletter_techdigest" in our ledger so we can reconcile spend easily.
- Send the CSV with codes + issuance date + expiry.

If marketing wants a clearer funnel, we can also add an internal tag so CS can proactively reach out to any redeemers above X usage in first 30 days.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success & Finance
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Promo codes for our Spring Roundup — quick ask

Quick legal check — nothing major. A few bullets to include in the campaign blurb and T&Cs:

- Codes are single-use and non-transferable.
- Must be redeemed by an account with a verified email.
- Redwood reserves the right to revoke codes in case of abuse; define abuse examples (automated redemptions, bulk account creation).
- No cash value; cannot be combined with other promotional credits.

If TechDigest wants us to generate codes tied to specific emails (i.e., reserved for contest winners), we’ll need to share a secure list in a signed SFTP or via encrypted Drive link — otherwise we’ll issue general single-use codes.

Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
